one_line_description.value: Slack connects teams and AI agents on an AI work platform.
one_line_description.quote: All your people and AI agents working together Slack connects your team.

has_public_api.quote: Documentation on event types and our Events API spec provide detail on specific event types.

api_type.quote: The Slack Web API featured workflows methods are now available!

api_breadth.value: Read-write access to channels/threads, messages, canvases, and search.
api_breadth.quote: Once connected, third-party AI agents can access your Slack workspace to read specific channels or threads, send messages, create canvases, and help you find information faster.

docs_url.quote: As previously announced, docs.slack.dev is the new home for Slack developer docs.

auth_methods.quote: Follow the prompts to review the scopes and install the app.

access_model.quote: You'll need to sign in to your Slack account to create an application.

access_notes.value: App creation requires a Slack account; workspace or Enterprise admins may require app approval before installation.
access_notes.quote: If app approval is required in your workspace or Enterprise organization, only admins and members with permission can install apps that include MCP servers.

official_mcp_server.quote: The Slack MCP server lets third-party AI agents like Claude and Perplexity securely access your Slack content so they can search messages, find information, and take actions in Slack on your behalf.

webhooks.quote: All delivered events follow this liberal JSON Schema specification.

sandbox_or_test_env.quote: Members of the Slack Developer Program can provision sandboxes to use for testing purposes.

sdk_languages.quote: The Bolt for JavaScript and Bolt for Python sample apps referenced in the documentation are now included in prompts of the `slack samples` command

api_versioning_or_deprecation_notes.value: Classic apps are deprecated; the deprecation date was pushed to November 16, 2026.
api_versioning_or_deprecation_notes.quote: We're pushing the deprecation date for classic apps to November 16, 2026.

verdict_reason: Slack publishes developer documentation at docs.slack.dev, app creation is self-serve after signing in to a Slack account, and the API supports read-write messaging, channels/threads, canvases, and search. An official Slack MCP server and developer sandboxes are also documented. No sales contact or partner approval is evidenced for development access.
open_questions: Auth mechanism is not explicitly named in the supplied pages; OAuth2 is inferred from documented app-install scope review, and the dedicated docs.slack.dev/authentication page was not included in SOURCES.
Rate limits are not documented in the supplied evidence; the 2026 rate-limits changelog text does not include limit numbers.
Slack MCP server endpoint URL is not published in the supplied evidence; the official help-center guide URL is used.
API versioning scheme is not evidenced; only the classic-app deprecation date is documented.
Community MCP servers were not found in the provided evidence.
Workspace/Enterprise app approval and sandbox provisioning can gate installation/testing; exact production review requirements are not fully documented in the evidence.
